ops.title: Task anchors deliberately carry no witness: a Task.Witness field is a trap, not a one-line fix
ops.body:
Tasks are gaining anchors (path/dir/commit) so they can reach code — note 3628756 measured 290/290 tasks with zero anchors, hence zero note<->task edges corpus-wide. Those anchors carry **no `AnchorWitness`** and therefore **cannot drift**. That is deliberate. This note exists because "just add a `Witness` field to `model.Task`" is the plausible-looking one-line change a future agent will reach for, and it is actively harmful.

## The trap: `verdictOf` short-circuits before it ever reaches drift

`verdictOf` (notes/document.go:869) evaluates in strict precedence order:

```
StaleAt != 0    -> EXPIRED
VerifiedAt == 0 -> UNVERIFIED      <-- returns here
head != ""      -> driftedOf(...)  -> DRIFTED
now - VerifiedAt > staleAfter      -> STALE
```

Its input is `freshDocument` (notes/document.go:848) = `{Anchors, Witness, VerifiedAt, StaleAt, SupersededBy}`. `model.Task` has **none** of `VerifiedAt`, `StaleAt`, `SupersededBy`.

So a task carrying a `Witness` but no verify lifecycle has `VerifiedAt == 0` forever. Every call returns `UNVERIFIED` and `driftedOf` is **unreachable**. The result is not "drift detection arrives late" — it is all tasks flagged UNVERIFIED permanently, with the witness computed, stored, and never read. It would look wired and be dead.

## Four supporting findings, each checked in source

1. **`buildWitness` has exactly one production caller.** `reVerify` (notes/document.go:214-225) does nothing but append `model.VerifyNote{Witness, VerifiedCommit}`. No path records a witness outside the verify op — not on create, not on anchor edit, for any kind. Notes and docs are "born verified" only because `createDocument` (notes/document.go:198) runs `reVerify` as a **second append** after `s.Create`.
2. **The dispatcher physically refuses non-documents.** `documentAnchors` (notes/document.go:228) ends in `default: panic("notes: reVerify on a non-document snapshot")`. Routing a task through the existing witness path is a panic, not a missing case.
3. **The op that writes a witness writes five other fields tasks lack.** `internal/fold/fold_note.go:84-89`, `case model.VerifyNote:` sets `VerifiedAt`, `VerifiedBy`, `VerifiedCommit`, the witness, and clears `StaleAt`/`StaleBy`/`StaleReason`. Folding `VerifyNote` on a task means adding all six fields to `model.Task`, plus a `task verify` verb that does not exist.
4. **Witness-less anchors are the established majority design.** Commit a467728 (2026-07-14) gave `model.Runbook` exactly `Anchors` and `Deleted` — no witness, no `VerifiedAt`. notes/relevant.go:64-67 states it outright: *"Notes and docs carry their content verdict; a log, runbook, or investigation never drifts, so its Verdict is empty."* Tasks are the fourth such kind, not an exception.

## Why tasks are outside the drift model by nature

Content drift is a **fact-shaped** signal. A note or doc asserts something about code that can silently become false; that is what a witness and a verify lifecycle exist to catch.

A task asserts **work to be done**. It does not become false when code moves — it becomes irrelevant by being closed, cancelled, or having its lease expire. The staleness design already carries the task-shaped signal separately (S5: task terminal or lease expired, off `SetStatus` and `StaleTasks(LeaseTTL)`). Giving a task a witness models it as a claim about the world rather than as a unit of work.

## The gap is theoretical, not real: check liveness at build time

The one thing anyone would genuinely want from a task witness is *"this task points at a path that no longer exists."* The graph builder does not need a stored witness for that. It rebuilds from scratch in under five seconds, so it can evaluate path liveness against the live tree at build time and mark the edge dangling then.

A **stored** witness exists to make drift detection *incremental* for long-lived facts read one at a time. A full rebuild does not have that problem. Prefer a build-time liveness check over a stored witness.

## If you still want task drift

It is a phase, not a field: 6 new `model.Task` fields, a `VerifyNote` case in `fold_task`, a `documentAnchors` arm (or a task-specific `reVerify`), a `freshFromTask` projection, a `Verdict` arm, and a decision about whether `task add` becomes a two-append born-verified create like notes/docs — which changes `CreateTask`'s commit shape and every task-create test. Design it against the staleness gate's actual requirements, not from the anchor side.
